item.title: Strong atmospheric river triggers flood watches and warnings in Washington and Oregon
item.description: Flood watches and warnings were issued across western Oregon and Washington on December 7, 2025, valid through December 12, as strong atmospheric river produces sustained rainfall, rising river levels and increasing landslide risk. Source

item.title: Impulsive X1.1 solar flare erupts from Region 4298
item.description: A major solar flare measuring X1.1 erupted from Active Region 4298 at 05:01 UTC on December 8, 2025. The event started at 04:49 and ended at 05:04 UTC. Source

item.title: Firefighter killed by falling tree amid NSW wildfires that destroyed over 20 homes
item.description: A 59-year-old firefighter from New South Wales National Parks and Wildlife Service died late Sunday, December 7, 2025, at Nerong, Bulahdelah after being struck by a falling tree while working on a wildfire burning across the state’s Mid North Coast. Source

item.title: Alberta Clipper prompts winter storm watches in Minnesota, Wisconsin, North Dakota, and Wyoming
item.description: A strong Alberta clipper will bring heavy snow and gusty winds to the northern Plains and Upper Midwest from Tuesday, December 9, through early Wednesday, December 10, 2025, prompting winter storm watches across multiple states. Source

item.title: Small meteotsunami observed across North Island coasts, New Zealand
item.description: A small meteotsunami was observed along New Zealand’s East Coast and Lake Taupō last week as a strong weather system swept across the upper North Island, GeoNet reported on December 8, 2025. Source

item.title: Major M7.6 earthquake hits near the coast of Hokkaido, Japan, hazardous tsunami waves possible
item.description: A major earthquake registered by the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and USGS as M7.6 struck off the east coast of Aomori Prefecture, Japan, at 14:15 UTC (23:15 JST) on December 8, 2025. Both agencies are reporting a depth of 50 km (31 miles). According to the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center (PTWC), hazardous tsunami waves are possible within 1 000 km (620 miles) of the epicenter. Source

item.title: Aurora forecast across northern U.S., southern Canada, and northern Europe on December 9
item.description: Auroras are expected across much of the northern United States, southern Canada, and northern Europe on December 9, 2025, following a forecasted geomagnetic disturbance caused by a coronal mass ejection (CME) produced during the December 6 M8.1 solar flare. Source

item.title: Medical shortages and disease cases rise as Cyclone Senyar death tolls climbs to 940, Indonesia
item.description: Health complications are spreading in flood-hit in the provinces of North Sumatra, West Sumatra, and Aceh, as medical facilities face severe disruptions. Officials confirm 940 deaths and 276 people missing following Cyclone Senyar’s impact in Indonesia as of Sunday, December 7. Source

item.title: Geminid meteor shower peaks on December 13–14 under favorable observing conditions
item.description: The exact moonrise time varies with longitude, so optimal viewing intervals depend on local conditions. After moonrise, observers can continue viewing by facing westward to minimize lunar glare. Source

item.title: Severe winds and hazardous seas forecast for Ireland and the UK as Storm Bram deepens
item.description: A rapidly deepening Atlantic low, named Storm Bram, is forecast to pass close to the western coasts of Ireland, Northern Ireland and the Outer Hebrides on Tuesday, December 9, 2025, bringing very strong southerly winds, heavy rain and exceptionally high seas. The system forms part of an active North Atlantic storm train linked to recent Polar Vortex disruption. Source
